recent_posts.title: Understanding Merkle Trees
recent_posts.summary: Merkle trees are hash-based data structures that efficiently verify data integrity and detect changes in large datasets. Each leaf node contains a hash of data (like a file), and parent nodes contain hashes of their children, culminating in a single root hash that represents the entire dataset. When data changes, only the affected path from leaf to root needs recalculation, enabling logarithmic-time verification. This makes them ideal for file synchronization (Dropbox, Git), blockchain transaction verification, distributed database consistency checks, and certificate transparency systems. The article walks through a detailed file sync example, explains performance characteristics (O(log n) for balanced trees), and covers real-world applications across cryptocurrencies, version control, distributed databases, and security systems.

recent_posts.title: Computer science degrees now teach critical thinking over job guarantees
recent_posts.summary: Computer science instructor Elisa Cundiff and Kirupa Chinnathambi explore whether CS degrees remain valuable as AI automates technical tasks and entry-level hiring shrinks. They discuss how AI has made cheating easier, why understanding fundamentals like data structures and algorithms still matters for auditing AI output, and how CS education now signals cognitive discipline over guaranteed job security. The conversation emphasizes that productive struggle and critical thinking remain essential skills, even as AI handles more coding tasks.

recent_posts.title: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) Explained
recent_posts.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables AI assistants to securely connect to real-world data, tools, and services. Described as the 'USB-C for LLMs,' MCP provides a universal bridge between large language models and external systems, addressing authentication, streaming, and standardization challenges that existing REST APIs don't solve. The protocol supports both local and hosted server implementations, features a public registry for discoverability, and maintains vendor neutrality across AI providers. MCP serves as foundational infrastructure for agentic workflows where users interact with systems through natural language commands rather than traditional interfaces.

recent_posts.title: Why domain expertise still matters in AI assisted coding
recent_posts.summary: AI-assisted coding (vibe coding) can significantly boost productivity by handling boilerplate and repetitive tasks, but the generated code often lacks quality and best practices. To maximize effectiveness, developers need deep domain expertise to identify issues, provide detailed prompts, and thoroughly review AI output. The combination of AI efficiency with human expertise in code quality creates the most powerful development workflow.

recent_posts.title: How to Count in Negabinary (Base (-2)) — A Visual Guide
recent_posts.summary: Negabinary (base -2) is a number system that uses powers of -2 instead of 2, allowing representation of both positive and negative numbers without sign bits. The conversion process from decimal to negabinary involves dividing by -2 and adjusting negative remainders by adding 1 to the quotient and 2 to the remainder. Converting back to decimal requires mapping each digit to its corresponding power of -2. A key insight is that you can determine if a negabinary number is positive or negative by checking the position of the leading bit - even positions indicate positive numbers, odd positions indicate negative numbers.

recent_posts.title: Do we need to understand technical details with AI?
recent_posts.summary: In a world dominated by AI, the necessity of understanding technical concepts like Bloom filters or traditional programming fundamentals is becoming questionable. recent_posts.title: Drawing Sharp Lines on the Canvas
recent_posts.summary: To ensure sharp and crisp lines on the HTML canvas, the positioning of lines based on their width is crucial. Odd-width lines should be placed on half-pixel values, while even-width lines should be on whole-pixel values. This method prevents blurriness caused by the canvas rendering engine's antialiasing. A live example is provided to demonstrate this concept in action.
